name: Remote Access Software

attack_mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

evidence.rationale: Application allowlisting prevents execution of unauthorized remote access tools (e.g., AnyDesk, TeamViewer, custom RATs). If not explicitly authorized, these binaries cannot execute, directly reducing adversary persistence and command-and-control capability.

Host firewall rules can block inbound or outbound communications associated with unauthorized remote access software. The firewall does not prevent the software from being installed or executed when it communicates over an allowed channel.

Application-aware or destination-restricted firewall policies can block communications to unauthorized remote-access services. Tools communicating through generally permitted HTTPS may bypass basic port filtering.

Secure software management can limit administration to approved and securely configured remote-access products. The safeguard does not prevent an approved tool or account from being abused by an adversary.
Removing unauthorized or unnecessary remote-access products and disabling embedded remote-support functionality directly eliminates those access channels.
Configure network firewalls and proxies at segment boundaries to restrict outgoing traffic to sites and services associated with unauthorized remote-access software.
Network intrusion prevention solutions can use network signatures to block traffic associated with unauthorized remote-access services.
Application firewalls and proxies can restrict access to websites, services, and destinations associated with unauthorized remote-access tools.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
